extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Picture subtitles stored inside a film's own file (VobSub) now appear in the subtitle list when the file plays directly. They used to be offered only burnt into the picture, which meant re-encoding the whole video for a subtitle track. Needs tofa server 0.9.33, which is now the version this add-on is built against. - Collections people make on your server now show up in Browse, ahead of the catalogue's own franchise sets. Open one to see what's in it; making and editing them stays in tofa's web app for now. Needs tofa server 0.9.33. - "Always show subtitles" no longer gives up when no track matches your preferred language: it now tries the language of the audio you are hearing, then a track with no language label, before leaving subtitles off. The same order tofa's web player uses. - A converted stream that cannot start straight away -- usually because a just-stopped stream is still letting go of the server's graphics card -- now gets a second chance two seconds later instead of an error message.
